name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Turkish lira near record lows under managed depreciation; no major EM default or capital controls
state: The Turkish lira has traded near record lows against the dollar in a managed depreciation after rate cuts and rising inflation (Trading Economics). The slide has been gradual rather than a 10% monthly fall, and searches on 7 Nov found no major emerging economy that had defaulted, imposed capital controls or sought emergency IMF support.
for_you: Gradual currency weakness raises import costs in the countries affected.
rubric_hit: No major EM in acute distress = Normal

sources.title: Trading Economics — Turkish lira hits new low
GlobalCapital — Turkey picks up as rest of EM lags

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
